title: Sharp Honest Interval Length for Binary Finite-Population Effects at Moderate-Deviation Error Levels
banked_reason: The advertised stringent-confidence crossover remains unresolved: neither the logarithmic correction nor the allocation-dependent coefficient is identified statistically, and the proved spectral optimization supplies neither correction-attaining intervals nor a matching correction-scale converse.
gap_reasons: The advertised stringent-confidence crossover remains unresolved: neither the logarithmic correction nor the allocation-dependent coefficient is identified statistically, and the proved spectral optimization supplies neither correction-attaining intervals nor a matching correction-scale converse. The broad-prior lower proof's interior truncation alone loses order n^(-23/60), larger than the diagnostic n^(-2/3) correction, so its remainder cannot support that expansion.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved exact whole-interval reduction, an all-procedure finite dual, finite connected honesty, a certified diagnostic spectral evaluator, the one-unit frontier, and the sharp compact-uniform leading constant. A maximality repair promoted the leading theorem and synchronized the prose, but the correction-sensitive Lemma M transfer remained open; D0.5 math passed while the decision referee found kernel_substituted and the general referee capped the result at incremental. No Lean formalization was launched; a future retry must establish the evaluated correction, smaller remainder, attaining connected procedure, and matching correction-scale converse without assuming the diagnostic operator transfer.
tldr: For arbitrary fixed binary potential outcomes, the minimum worst-table expected length over every outcome-independent design and every globally honest randomized original-record connected interval satisfies \(\ell_n(\lambda)=2\sqrt{2\lambda}n^{-1/3}+o_H(n^{-1/3})\) at error \(e^{-\lambda n^{1/3}}\), uniformly on every fixed positive compact parameter interval and for even and odd sample sizes. An explicit deterministic interval under fair independent assignment has finite-sample coverage at every size and attains this leading term. Whole-interval reduction, rational connected calibration, finite all-procedure lower bounds, the independent nonlocal spectral identity, supplied-tolerance spectral certification, and the one-unit formula are proved. The sharp logarithmic and allocation-dependent correction is the open question; the evaluated diagnostic operator is not yet a statistical coefficient.
gap: Unrestricted squared-risk optimality, exact causal interval algorithms, and exponentially accurate interval minimality use different loss or coverage criteria. They do not evaluate \(\ell_n(\lambda)\) to a correction-smaller remainder under the specified shrinking error budget.
fill: The contribution is an evaluated two-sided precision frontier over the original decision class, an exact connected attaining algorithm, and a terminating scalar or operator evaluator linked to effective finite upper and lower certificates.
